positioning: One machine-service factory, organized into human-readable service families.
truth_rule: Category pages describe real factory capabilities and measured status. A category or service is never labeled publicly live until activation gates pass.

categories.name: Research & Intelligence
categories.short: Turn open-world information into bounded, sourced machine outcomes.
categories.thesis: This family packages search, retrieval, source normalization, synthesis and qualification into outcomes a machine can buy without assembling its own research stack.
examples: Research a market and return a sourced brief
Find organizations matching a declared business profile
Synthesize permitted external sources into a structured answer
categories.contract_pattern: Declare the question or target, scope, requested fields and evidence requirements. CommandLayer returns structured output, source provenance, explicit unknowns and execution evidence.
boundaries: No guarantee of factual truth
No unlawful sensitive-person targeting
No invented contact or source fields
Provider/source failures remain visible

services.name: ResearchAgent
services.evidence: 2/25 accepted in the latest provider-backed reliability window; Firecrawl availability is the current blocker.
services.job: Answer a bounded research question from permitted external sources and return a structured result with source provenance and execution evidence.
services.returns: structured answer + sources + uncertainty + execution evidence

services.name: LeadAgent
services.evidence: 8/25 accepted across the latest provider-backed reliability window; intermittent structured-model failures remain under repair.
services.job: Produce a bounded list of organizations or professional contacts matching declared business criteria, with qualification evidence and provenance.
services.inputs: ideal customer profile + geography/market + requested fields
services.returns: qualified entities + explicit unknowns + field provenance

categories.name: Search, Crawl & Retrieval
categories.short: Acquire permitted external resources inside explicit machine-readable bounds.
categories.thesis: Retrieval services are the acquisition layer beneath many higher-value outcomes. They enforce scope, redirects, limits, network safety, provider accounting and observable failures instead of exposing an unconstrained browser or crawler.
examples: Crawl a bounded set of pages and return content hashes
Fetch a declared resource without following unsafe redirects
Acquire source material for a composed research or comparison task
categories.contract_pattern: Declare start URLs/resources and bounds. The service records every attempted resource, status, redirects, coverage and successful content hashes.
boundaries: No credential or access-control bypass
No unrestricted site mirroring
Explicit page/time/resource limits
Blocked and failed resources are never reported as successful

services.name: CrawlAgent
services.evidence: Live Firecrawl calls succeeded at about $0.005 variable COGS; prior five-sample run reached 2/5 because of HTTP 429s. Retry-After hardening is built and awaits paced confirmation.
services.job: Retrieve permitted web resources within explicit crawl bounds and return normalized fetch results, status metadata and content hashes.
services.returns: resource statuses + normalized content + hashes + coverage summary

categories.name: Documents & Data Extraction
categories.short: Convert supplied documents and content into declared machine schemas.
categories.thesis: This family turns documents, text and structured inputs into normalized machine data while preserving source anchors, hashes, unreadable fields and acceptance rules.
examples: Extract invoice fields into a declared schema
Parse supplied content into normalized JSON
Classify a document and preserve source anchors for every material field
categories.contract_pattern: Supply authorized content plus the target schema. CommandLayer hashes the input, parses deterministically where possible, uses model/document providers only when needed, validates output and exposes unreadable fields rather than inventing values.
boundaries: No fabricated unreadable values
No authenticity claim without a separate verification contract
Schema failures are terminal unless the contract allows degraded output
Private documents must be supplied or authorized

services.name: DocumentAgent
services.evidence: 25/25 provider-backed acceptance; aggregate p95 variable COGS about $0.004036; current pre-production launch recommendation $0.49.
services.job: Extract, classify and structure information from supplied or authorized documents into a declared schema with source anchors and execution evidence.
services.returns: validated structured fields + anchors + coverage + document hash

services.name: ParseAgent
services.evidence: 5/5 deterministic acceptance with zero measured vendor COGS on the tested path; current pre-production launch recommendation $0.10.
services.job: Transform supplied content into a declared structured representation using deterministic parsing first.
services.returns: validated representation + parse mode + input/output hashes

categories.name: Analysis, Comparison & Decisioning
categories.short: Normalize alternatives and expose how a machine reached a decision surface.
categories.thesis: Decision services should make criteria, missing data, normalization and weighting visible. CommandLayer packages those mechanics into bounded outcomes rather than returning an unexplained recommendation.
examples: Compare three vendors against declared criteria
Normalize plan features while leaving unavailable values missing
Score alternatives using an exposed weighting formula
categories.contract_pattern: Declare alternatives, criteria and optional weights. The result includes a normalized matrix, provenance or missing markers for material fields, and the scoring formula when scoring is requested.
boundaries: No hidden preference injection
No claim of an objective best choice without declared weighting
Missing values remain missing unless imputation is explicitly requested
No irreversible purchase action inside the comparison contract

services.name: CompareAgent
services.evidence: 25/25 provider-backed acceptance; aggregate p95 variable COGS about $0.00737425; current pre-production launch recommendation $0.49.
services.job: Compare declared alternatives against explicit criteria and return a normalized decision matrix with source provenance and missing-data disclosure.
services.returns: comparison matrix + normalization rules + provenance + optional scoring

categories.name: Monitoring, Tracking & State
categories.short: Observe external state over time and preserve what changed, when and from where.
categories.thesis: Long-lived agent workflows need durable state, not just stateless requests. This family stores observations and snapshots separately from failures so a bad fetch cannot overwrite the last known good state.
examples: Watch a page and emit an evidenced change event
Track a metric and retain snapshot history
Detect no-change as a valid observation rather than a failure
categories.contract_pattern: Declare a target, observation/tracking specification and cadence or trigger. Successful observations are hashed and linked to prior state; failed observations are recorded separately and never masquerade as no-change.
boundaries: No guarantee of future detection
No fabricated no-change event when fetch fails
No hidden private-system access
Irreversible response actions require a separate authorization contract

services.name: MonitorAgent
services.evidence: 5/5 on the tested synchronous measurement path at about 128 ms p95 and zero vendor COGS. Launch recommendation remains provisional until async queue/scheduler timing and trust gates clear.
services.job: Observe a declared external target over time and emit durable, evidenced change events when state changes or a declared condition is met.
services.returns: observation state + before/after evidence + timestamps + hashes

services.name: TrackAgent
services.evidence: 5/5 on the tested synchronous measurement path at about 120 ms p95 and zero vendor COGS. Launch recommendation remains provisional until async queue/scheduler timing and trust gates clear.
services.job: Maintain durable snapshots for a declared entity or metric and return current state, history references and evidenced changes.
services.returns: current snapshot + prior reference + change state + hashes

categories.name: Verification, Trust & Provenance
categories.short: Verify execution evidence without pretending a signature proves truth.
categories.thesis: Machines need an independent way to verify what executed, which signer produced the evidence and what proof scope the receipt actually covers. CommandLayer deliberately separates cryptographic execution evidence from factual truth.
examples: Verify a signed execution receipt
Resolve the declared signer and public key
Return VERIFIED, INVALID or INDETERMINATE with machine-readable checks
categories.contract_pattern: Submit a supported receipt/artifact. Verification canonicalizes it, validates schema and hashes, resolves the trusted signer key, verifies the Ed25519 signature and reports every check independently.
boundaries: Signature validity is not factual truth
Unsupported profiles return INDETERMINATE
Failed checks cannot be hidden behind VERIFIED
Identity resolution is scoped to the declared proof surface

services.name: VerifyAgent
services.evidence: Factory verification and HTTPS trust-root resolution are built and released in code. The deployed signed-receipt round trip remains blocked on the real non-exportable production signer/public key.
services.job: Verify integrity, signer/provenance and declared proof scope of a supported artifact without claiming the underlying statement is factually true.

categories.name: Identity, Access & Authorization
categories.short: Bind who or what may act to explicit machine-readable scopes.
categories.thesis: Identity answers who a machine or service claims to be; authorization answers what it may do. CommandLayer keeps these separate from settlement and execution evidence so permission is explicit rather than inferred from possession of a wallet or API key.
examples: Resolve a service or agent identity
Evaluate a bounded action mandate
Attach spend, resource and time scopes before execution
categories.contract_pattern: Identity and authorization adapters can contribute scoped claims to an execution request, but the factory still evaluates service-specific policy before admitting work.
boundaries: Identity does not imply authorization
Payment does not imply authorization
High-consequence actions require explicit scope
Replay and expiry are part of authorization semantics

categories.name: Commerce, Payments & Settlement
categories.short: Let machines obtain a price, settle and invoke without a human checkout flow.
categories.thesis: Machine commerce needs price discovery, bounded payment, idempotent settlement and atomic admission. CommandLayer treats x402 and other payment systems as settlement adapters around the service contract—not as the product itself.
examples: Receive HTTP 402 payment requirements
Settle a bounded USDC amount and retry the request
Admit execution only after settlement evidence passes factory policy
categories.contract_pattern: A buyer requests a priced service, receives payment requirements when settlement is required, pays on an allowed rail and retries with payment evidence. Admission remains idempotent and service-policy aware.
boundaries: Payment proof is not execution proof
Allowed network/asset/payee are explicit
Cumulative and per-payment spend controls are enforced
Refund/payout/purchase actions remain separately permissioned

categories.name: Communication & Messaging
categories.short: Deliver machine-to-machine or machine-to-human messages with explicit destinations and evidence.
categories.thesis: Communication services turn notifications, responses and delivery workflows into bounded operations rather than giving an agent unrestricted access to a messaging account.
examples: Send a notification to an authorized destination
Route a response through a declared channel
Return delivery status and provider evidence
categories.contract_pattern: The caller declares destination, channel, content constraints and authorization. The service records provider delivery state and never upgrades an attempted delivery into a confirmed delivery without evidence.
boundaries: Destination authorization is explicit
No credential harvesting
No false delivery confirmation
Bulk or unsolicited messaging requires service-specific abuse controls

categories.name: Workflow, Scheduling & Operations
categories.short: Coordinate durable jobs, schedules and bounded operational steps.
categories.thesis: Autonomous systems need durable execution semantics: leases, retries, schedules, idempotency, recovery and observable terminal states. This family exposes those operational outcomes without handing buyers the entire internal runtime.
examples: Schedule a bounded recurring observation
Run an asynchronous job with durable status
Coordinate a composed workflow with retry and terminal-state evidence
categories.contract_pattern: A workflow contract declares the job, schedule or trigger, retry policy, idempotency scope and terminal conditions. Durable state separates successful work from failed attempts.
boundaries: No unbounded recurrence
Retries remain inside budget and idempotency scope
Failed attempts cannot overwrite last-good state
Irreversible steps require their own authorization

categories.name: Media, Transformation & Utility
categories.short: Transform supplied media and content into machine-usable representations.
categories.thesis: Utility services are composable building blocks for higher-value outcomes. They are useful when the transformation itself is the product and when another service needs a dependable primitive underneath.
examples: Transcribe supplied audio into timestamped text
Normalize media-derived segments
Expose hashes and provider provenance for transformed media
categories.contract_pattern: Supply authorized media plus requested output options. The service records media hashes, provider steps, ordered segments and coverage; unintelligible spans remain explicit.
boundaries: No speaker-identity guarantee without separate evidence
No unauthorized private media
Low-quality spans are marked rather than invented
Provider retries remain bounded by quote and timeout

services.name: TranscribeAgent
services.evidence: A bounded inline MP3 fixture is bundled into the canonical measurement matrix and secure-ingestion checks pass. Live transcription measurement remains pending.
services.job: Transcribe supplied or authorized audio/video into timestamped text and optional structured segments with provider provenance and media hashes.
services.returns: ordered transcript segments + timestamps + language state + media hash

categories.name: Developer, Infrastructure & Agent Operations
categories.short: Expose the factory surfaces machines and developers use to integrate, discover and operate services.
categories.thesis: The infrastructure family covers the machinery around outcomes: manifests, schemas, discovery adapters, metering, execution ledgers, receipts, telemetry, provider routing and compatibility surfaces such as HTTP/JSON, OpenAPI, MCP, x402 and future agent directories.
examples: Read a canonical machine service manifest
Integrate through HTTP/JSON or a supported adapter
Inspect quote, execution, telemetry and receipt surfaces
categories.contract_pattern: The canonical service definition is authoritative. External protocols and directories are adapters around that definition so the contract does not fork by distribution channel.
boundaries: Adapters do not become competing sources of truth
Provider routing is cost/control infrastructure, not the product moat
Telemetry cannot overstate organic demand
Experimental adapters are labeled as such
